author: NewsBreak
title: U.S. Treasury Ends Paper Checks for Payments Impacting Social Security, Veterans Benefits Nationwide - NewsBreak
text:
4 hours ago WASHINGTON, D.C. – Major changes are on the horizon for millions of Americans who still receive federal payments by paper check. Beginning September 30, 2025, the federal government will no longer issue paper checks for most federal payments, shifting instead to safer, faster electronic options.
Photo by Brands&People on Unsplash “With paper checks over 16 times more likely to get lost, stolen, altered, or delayed, we encourage those still receiving paper checks to make the switch today,” said Fiscal Service Chief Disbursing Officer Linda Chero. “Electronic payments such as direct deposit are safer than checks, allow quicker access to funds, and have less risk of fraud.”
For those already receiving federal benefits or tax refunds electronically, no action is needed. But individuals who still get Social Security or Veterans benefits by paper check are urged to sign up for direct deposit. Enrollment options include contacting the paying agency directly, visiting GoDirect.gov, or calling the Electronic Payment Solution Center at 800-967-6857, Monday through Friday.
People without a bank account can explore options at FDIC.gov/GetBanked or MyCreditUnion.gov. Another choice is the Direct Express® debit card, a Treasury-sponsored card that allows recipients to securely receive benefits without a traditional bank account.
Government vendors are also required to update their SAM.gov registration with current bank account details. The help desk is available at 866-606-8220 for assistance.
Officials warn the public to be alert for scams as the deadline approaches. Individuals should verify requests through trusted agency websites or official phone numbers before responding.
The Treasury urges anyone still using paper checks not to wait. Enrolling in electronic payments now can help avoid delays and ensure uninterrupted access to federal funds.
